problem: Open VLN models such as StreamVLN (8.03B params, 16.1 GB in BF16) do not fit memory- and power-limited edge boards like the Jetson Orin NX 16GB. Compression alone does not show that a model meets edge memory, latency and energy budgets while keeping closed-loop navigation behavior.
motivation: Offloading navigation to a server adds latency, needs persistent connectivity, and sends the robot's camera views off-board. The authors observe that bit width does not predict peak memory, latency or energy, because runtime, KV cache and dequantization path dominate. They also observe that the SR-OSR gap stays nearly constant across viable precisions, so wrong stopping comes from the base model, not from quantization.
key_idea: Deploy a 4-bit (IQ4_NL) StreamVLN through a custom llama.cpp VLN driver, and use the memory and latency freed by quantization for LATTE, a small causal-transformer stop verifier that reads the backbone's layer-24 hidden states.
insight: Runtime choice matters more than bit width: 4-bit formats have near-identical SR (within 0.54 points of BF16), but per-step energy varies 36.8x (IQ4_NL 11.41 J vs INT4 419.70 J) and peak RAM ranges from 11.35 to 15.85 GB. For stop verification, the input matters: heads on pooled vision features lose SR (MLP-vision 51.70, concat 45.79 on BF16), while heads on decoder hidden states gain (L20 58.24, L24 58.13). Causal attention over hidden states (LATTE) is best at half the size (8.2 MB vs 15.7 MB), raising SR while lowering OSR, which shows it fixes termination rather than path-following.
method: Base agent: frozen StreamVLN (SigLIP-SO400M, 2-layer MLP projector, Qwen2 28 layers, d=3584, 8.03B params) with a sliding-window dialogue KV cache and stride-sampled memory tokens.

Selective quantization: quantizes only the LM feed-forward blocks (5.70B of 8.03B params); the vision tower, projector, attention projections, embeddings and LM head stay at 16-bit. Precisions are first swept with fake quantization to isolate precision from runtime.

llama.cpp VLN driver: exports the vision tower and projector to multimodal GGUF, re-implements the 27x27->14x14 pooling (196 tokens per frame), clears context every 32 steps and re-injects stride-sampled earlier frames as raw embedding batches. No deep-learning framework is in the inference path.

On-board voxel memory-token pruning: each token cell takes its median depth, is back-projected to a voxel, and only the most recent token per voxel per temporal bucket is kept. It is applied only at chunk boundaries and removes 41.7% of re-injected tokens, cutting amortized step time from 0.744 to 0.672 s.

LATTE head: mean-pools the 196 image-token rows of layer-24 hidden states per frame into a 3584-d feature, buffers up to 256 steps (averaged over 16), and projects to d=256. Two pre-norm causal transformer layers (4 heads, FFN 512) with a sigmoid output regress goal_rank_camera_height = clip(1-d_t/5m,0,1) under an MSE loss. The head is trained on 3184 successful rollouts from the R2R VLN-CE train split, is kept in FP32, and runs on the CPU.

Hysteresis stop trigger: tracks the running maximum of the rank and issues STOP once the maximum exceeds a threshold and the current score has dropped by a fixed margin, with a minimum step count. Threshold and margin are chosen by a 16-cell grid search per backbone.

setting.backbone: StreamVLN (SigLIP-SO400M + Qwen2-7B LLM, 8.03B), post-training quantized (IQ4_NL deployed) + LATTE causal transformer stop head
setting.training_data: StreamVLN pretrained weights, frozen and quantized post-training with no retraining; LATTE trained on features from 3184 successful R2R VLN-CE train rollouts (2548/318/318 split)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (a placeholder pose and zero depth in RGB-only VLN-CE), 32-frame KV context, plus instruction
setting.action_space: low-level discrete actions (move forward, turn left, turn right, stop), generated as 4-action chunks
setting.simulator: Habitat (R2R VLN-CE); on-board latency/energy measured on a Jetson Orin NX 16GB by replaying a recorded real-world 89-frame episode
setting.privileged: none at test time (LATTE's training targets use GT goal distance); stop trigger thresholds were tuned on the val-unseen episodes reported, so the gain is an upper bound

numbers.extra: Threshold/margin tuned on the same val-unseen episodes (upper bound); RGB-only; LATTE trained on 3184 train rollouts; on-board: RAM 11.35 GB, 11.54 J/step, 0.69 s/step on Jetson Orin NX

numbers_note: Only SR and OSR are reported (no SPL, NE or nDTW). BF16 baseline (StreamVLN) is 57.69 SR / 65.04 OSR. Full 1,839 val-unseen episodes were evaluated.
results: On all 1,839 R2R-CE val-unseen episodes, the IQ4_NL model keeps SR at 57.31 vs 57.69 for BF16, and LATTE raises it to 58.02 (+0.71), above the BF16 baseline. On the Jetson Orin NX the deployed model uses 11.35 GB, runs 20.8x faster and uses 13.3x less energy per step than storage-streamed BF16, with LATTE adding only 0.013 s and 0.13 J per step.
limitations: LATTE's threshold and margin were tuned on the same val-unseen episodes reported, so the SR gain is an upper bound; the +0.71 gain is small and head differences are below run-to-run spread.
On-board cost is measured by replaying a single recorded 89-frame real-world episode with a stationary robot, not in closed-loop real-world navigation; the closed-loop SR comes from Habitat only.
RGB-only setting where voxel pruning is effectively inactive in sim; only one board (Orin NX) and one base model (StreamVLN) are studied; INT2 collapses.
